issue.title: `click.Path` should be generic on `path_type`
issue.body:
Click 8.5.0 made `click.prompt` and `click.ParamType` generic, so the return type of `click.prompt` is now normally clever enough to reveal the actual type of the value as converted from raw input.

However, `click.Path` has a `path_type` parameter to which the input is converted, but  that information is not reflected in the return type of `click.Path.convert`, so it's always typed as `str | bytes | os.PathLike[str]`, regardless of the value of `path_type`.

```python
# mre.py
import pathlib

from typing_extensions import assert_type

import click

my_type = click.Path(file_okay=False, path_type=pathlib.Path)
path = click.prompt("Enter a name", type=my_type)

# expected: pathlib.Path, actual: str | bytes | os.PathLike[str]
assert_type(path, pathlib.Path)
```

I checked the above MRE with mypy and pyright, as well as ty for completeness, on a local clone of the repo @ `main`:

```console
$ uv run mypy mre.py
mre.py:12: error: Expression is of type "str | bytes | PathLike[str]", not "Path"  [assert-type]
    assert_type(path, pathlib.Path)
    ^
Found 1 error in 1 file (checked 1 source file)
```

```console
$ uv run pyright mre.py
WARNING: there is a new pyright version available (v1.1.408 -> v1.1.411).
Please install the new version or set PYRIGHT_PYTHON_FORCE_VERSION to `latest`

/Users/edgarramirez/Contrib/pallets/click/mre.py
  /Users/edgarramirez/Contrib/pallets/click/mre.py:12:13 - error: "assert_type" mismatch: expected "Path" but received "str | bytes | os.PathLike[str]" (reportAssertTypeFailure)
1 error, 0 warnings, 0 informations
```

```console
$ uv run ty check mre.py
error[type-assertion-failure]: Argument does not have asserted type `Path`
  --> mre.py:12:1
   |
12 | assert_type(path, pathlib.Path)
   | ^^^^^^^^^^^^----^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
   |             |
   |             Inferred type is `str | bytes | os.PathLike[str]`
info: `Path` and `str | bytes | os.PathLike[str]` are not equivalent types

Found 1 diagnostic
```

I expect the return type of `click.prompt` to match the `path_type` value passed to `click.Path`.

Environment:

- Python version: 3.14
- Click version: 8.5.0

arms.better: tm found the relevant typing and prompt files, but repeatedly reread the same source and did not turn that investigation into an edit or a targeted check; the run ended escalated with no submission. Its user-facing messages were candid that no work was submitted, but terms such as ‘focused continuation’ and ‘provider transport retries’ are internal jargon, and the final instruction offered both `tm --resume S-3` and `tm ticket retry T-1` without explaining which action would preserve the current session versus restart ticket work. Reduce repeated file reads across continuation attempts, require the continuation to choose a concrete next action after the initial investigation, and end with one plain-language recommended recovery path plus the state of any retained edits.

OpenCode stated a scoped plan, found the implementation and typing-test locations quickly, corrected a mypy issue after an initial failure, and ran useful tests. It nevertheless missed important default-`click.Path()` cases: after the PR tests were applied, pytest passed (8 passed, 1 skipped), but both mypy and pyright failed on `tests/typing/typing_path.py` because the generic type variable has no default; the PR-added runtime genericity test also fails. It would be better to run the actual Path typing test file and runtime-generic test before finishing, ensure the generic preserves the prior default result type, and report the failure instead of treating only the narrower checks as sufficient.
